target_customer: Adults over 50, later sold through Medicare Advantage and other health plans
problem: Older adults lack fitness and nutrition programs designed for them. Mighty Health offered an app with a paired coach to help maintain daily function and healthy aging.
business_model: Consumer subscription, later B2B2C contracts with health plans
product_category: Digital health coaching for older adults

founders.name: James Li
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch July 2020 says he conceived the app after his father needed emergency open heart surgery.

founders.name: Bernard Chang
founders.background_notes: Emergency medicine doctor and vice chair of research at Columbia University Medical Center per TechCrunch.

exit.reason: Cause not public. YC lists Inactive while some third party profiles still describe the business as active.

technical_complexity.rationale: A coaching app with messaging, content and tracking is standard mobile engineering; the harder parts were clinical programming and health plan integration.

defensibility.rationale: Coach relationships and health plan contracts add some stickiness, but the app format was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying Mighty Health; SilverSneakers GO remained a fitness library incumbent.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2020 said mainstream fitness technology was not designed with older adults in mind, and the company targeted Medicare Advantage plans that cover millions of seniors.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positive, empowering tone for older adults

branding.community_and_virality: AARP Innovation Labs backed the company and TechCrunch covered the launch.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly name with AARP association and press, but no distinct mascot or community found.

pivots.from: Direct to consumer app for adults over 50
pivots.to: Virtual care platform sold to Medicare Advantage and commercial health plans
pivots.why: Third party profile (Village) describes health plan partnerships; the date is approximate and unconfirmed

outcome_analysis: Mighty Health raised $2.8 million in 2020 and $7.6 million in January 2023 while moving toward Medicare Advantage health plans, but the YC directory lists it as Inactive. No announcement of a shutdown, acquisition or layoffs was found, so the cause of the inactive status is not public and conflicting third party profiles still show it active.
notes: The 2023 round is reported by HIT Consultant and Axios (called a second seed round co-led by Will Ventures and GFT Ventures); Dealroom labels it Series A, so the stage conflicts and the article label seed is used. Aggregators show totals of $11.17M (CB Insights) and $11.75M (Caplight), above the $10.4M in recorded rounds, so earlier amounts may be missing, for example pre-batch angel money. The HIT Consultant and Axios pages were seen only in search snippets and not opened. The pivot date is approximate. Competitor list empty because the only dated source found (TechCrunch 2020) names none. Founder education not found. Conflict: YC says Inactive but Craft and Village show active.
